## R Markdown

This is an R Markdown document. Markdown is a simple formatting syntax for authoring HTML, PDF, and MS Word documents. For more details on using R Markdown see <http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com>.

When you click the **Knit** button a document will be generated that includes both content as well as the output of any embedded R code chunks within the document. You can embed an R code chunk like this:

```{r cars}
summary(cars)
```

## Including Plots

You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r pressure, echo=FALSE}
plot(pressure)
```

Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.

## Part A — Creating Vectors: c(), seq(), rep()
```{r}
scores <- c(88, 92, 79, 95, 84)
subjects <- c("English", "History", "PE")

rep("A", times = 4)
rep(c("A", "B"), each = 2 )
rep(c("A", "B"), times = 2)
```
Q1. Set up a vector named age, consisting of 15, 28, 32, 36, 27, 18, 52, 39, 42, 29, 35, 31, 27, 22, 37, 34, 19, 20, 57, 49, 50, 37, 46, 25, 17, 12, 42, 53, 41, 51, 35, 24, 33, 8.
```{r}
age <- c(15, 28, 32, 36, 27, 18, 52, 39, 42, 29, 35, 31, 27, 22, 37, 34, 19, 20, 57, 49, 50, 37, 46, 25, 17, 12, 42, 53, 41, 51, 35, 24, 33, 8)
length(age)
1 / age

new_age <- c(age, 0, age)
min(age)
max(age)
```
a. How many data points?
  34
b. Find the reciprocal of age?
  [1] 0.06666667 0.03571429 0.03125000 0.02777778 0.03703704
 [6] 0.05555556 0.01923077 0.02564103 0.02380952 0.03448276
[11] 0.02857143 0.03225806 0.03703704 0.04545455 0.02702703
[16] 0.02941176 0.05263158 0.05000000 0.01754386 0.02040816
[21] 0.02000000 0.02702703 0.02173913 0.04000000 0.05882353
[26] 0.08333333 0.02380952 0.01886792 0.02439024 0.01960784
[31] 0.02857143 0.04166667 0.03030303 0.12500000
c. Assign also new_age <- c(age, 0, age). What happens to new_age?
  It adds a single 0 in the middle of age. This creates a single elongated vector with a total length of 69 data points 34 + 1 + 34.
